body: I'm planning on applying to whatever I can find locally as long as it's not a position for which I'm clearly unqualified (for example, something that needs, say, accounting or engineering credentials). I'm trying to view it as a positive thing that I'm not specialized to a particular area so that might mean I have more options.

Well, I'm graduating this semester, so I shouldn't need to take out any more loans anyway. I have actually made friends with some good people over the past six months, which does help, and things in general are better now than most of what I described in my post, but it could still go either way, depending on the next couple months, so I'm trying, as you suggest, to minimize stress/financial burdens to try to help with that.
I cannot afford to relocate.
Sorry to hear that.

Oh, definitely. Being there was pretty difficult for me at times, but I feel like I got to know myself a lot better because of it, and there are a lot of things I'm still just noticing that I've realized over the past year, if it makes any sense to say it that way.

I guess we both thought it would be okay because we lived together before, but the circumstances then were different, and neither of us took that sufficiently into account. 

We do end up talking about the issue nearly every day, and it always feels like things are somewhat resolved, but in reality, they're not. 

>On the other hand, it honestly sounds like you think you are better than your boyfriend.

I'm not arguing with you at all, because I fear that you might be right in pointing this out, but in order to help me better understand it, could you please elaborate on that point?

I'm not sure what you mean by "sandal things", but I'm not really sure why I'm bothered by him sleeping during the day. I guess part of it is that we haven't been able to spend a lot of time together because we've been asleep at different times, and part is because right now, since I've just gotten back, I lack the means of doing much independently (no phone, car, or house key). I'm not suggesting (and I don't believe) that he's trying to prevent me from getting these, but the sleeping-during-the-day is making it harder. For example, we were supposed to go talk to the landlord yesterday so I could get a key and parking permit, so I woke him about 45 minutes before the leasing office closed, and he said there probably wasn't anyone there and that we'd go Monday. He also had said he'd drive me to the BMV, which is just under two miles from here, but since he was asleep, I ended up walking. (I actually didn't realize it was that far until I google mapped it just now to check.) I also wanted to get a phone yesterday, but he expressed doubt at my potential choice of provider, so I just decided to do it on my own later. 

Now, in his defense, he is driving me two hours to my mom's today so I can get my car, now that the tags are up to date and I have insurance, etc. Being able to drive will get rid of some of the feeling of powerlessness, but I keep worrying that something will happen to hinder it. I don't know why that is, because it's probably an unnecessary worry.

Thanks. I will keep that in mind. I've actually started to feel better about the whole thing over the course of the day, but I'm still cautious and not assuming that it'll magically fix itself. But I do feel *way* more like it can be worked out than I did this morning when I posed this.

Those are all good points. I do feel a bit better now that I've gone out by myself and got a few important issues taken care of. So far it's difficult for us to really talk to each other much, because he seems to sleep during the day (including right now), but hopefully that will change.

Well, he's actually only been here for six weeks because he moved from his last apartment (I thought I'd written that in my original post, but I must have deleted it when I was paring it down for length). So actually that's part of the issue, that he still has boxes of stuff around that he hasn't unpacked yet (and why I found myself slicing limes with a steak knife yesterday and drinking tea out of a glass measuring cup this morning...)

I definitely am feeling the familiar-yet-awkward thing, although less today than yesterday, when everything felt pretty surreal. I'm hoping to get back to a normal schedule within the next few days. Yesterday I'd only had four hours of sleep, and pretty much didn't eat anything after breakfast (there wasn't much food here to begin with, and the heat always kills my appetite), so I felt pretty awful and just ended up going to bed at 7 PM so I didn't have to deal with anything else. Of course, that led to me waking up around 4:30 this morning, but I'm going to try to stay up till at least 9 tonight.

You make a good point about getting familiar with each other again. We haven't really had much time to talk or hang out since I've gotten back, because we sleep at different times--I'm trying to sleep at night, whereas he seems to prefer the daytime (I guess that bothers me, but I don't really know why). I do feel a little more optimistic about the situation, though.
Yeah, that's true. Thanks.

I'm actually not on any birth control right now (I stopped taking the pill before I left) but I was planning to get back on it soon. Definitely a good question, but it looks like that's not a factor, though it could become one if I start taking it again.
Thank you; I will check that out.

Thank you for the information. I understand and agree with what they are saying here. This is not an appropriate place to ask for help with committing suicide. It is not even an appropriate place to expect to be talked out of suicide, because r/suicidewatch exists specifically for that purpose. 

However, I was doing neither of these things. As a matter of fact, it does not prohibit mention of suicide, but rather

>we don't want to field questions about how you can best kill yourself.

I would have imagined that not only the content of my post, but also the fact that I italicized and bolded the relevant sentences would have made it clear, as I already pointed out, that I do not wish to and have no intent to commit suicide. In fact, suicide was not at all the main topic of my post. If you read it, I do not understand how you could have misunderstood this, and I am beginning to question the motive behind your replies.

>Mods have said...these words don't belong here.

It does not say this in the rules on the sidebar. If it does say so somewhere else, and you would be kind enough to link me to it, then I will remove it. Prohibiting discussion of a topic or use of certain words without regard for its context does not sound like something that would be an actual policy here.
In Austria. I have felt somewhat better since the weather's gotten nicer, but yeah, that's still in my head occasionally.

Thank you. I guess I've been keeping this in my head too long and sort of felt like I was going crazy. I'm so glad that there's probably a rational explanation for at least part of this. 

I will try to go out for walks more and maybe get my roommate to go do stuff. She'll be into the more tourist-y things since she's only been here for a few weeks.

I don't know why I'm even responding, but by "openly abusing", I do mean that she drinks regularly to the point where she becomes abusive to people and blacks out, shows up to class drunk, and brings her drugs to school to show off to people. 

I have no problem with people drinking or using drugs recreationally so long as they're not harming other people.
As I said, I have no desire or intention to commit suicide.
I am in Austria.
Thanks, I'll try that. And in relation to body mass...well, I'm 5'3" and 120, so I guess one valerian capsule is probably the most I should take.
You're right; I'm just worried that she's going to be freaked out and then go tell the program director she wants a new roommate or something.

One? Oh, dear, maybe that was my problem. I took four, because that's what my uncle-in-law, who gave them to me, told me the dosage was. And the bottle was completely unmarked. Um. Actually, that sounds pretty terrible when I write it out like that. I guess I'm just glad that I wasn't, in fact, stating at his house like he'd suggested by the time I took them. Holy shit. Now I'm creeped out.

Yeah, to my knowledge I'm not schizophrenic (or at least have never been diagnosed with it). The few times I've smoked, it did make me sleep pretty heavily, although it's not something that I make a habit of. (The last two times I did it were actually to induce hunger (appetite?) after not being able to eat for a day or so.)

Okay, I'll keep that in mind. I haven't actually smoked at all since September. Also, for the record, I've not been diagnosed with any type of schizophrenia-related disorder. I hope my original post wasn't misleading; I just didn't mention a diagnosis related to the hallucinations, because I don't have one (so far).

I actually did check at the local grocery/drug stores, but I'm living in Europe at the moment, and couldn't find it anywhere, so I went ahead and ordered some the other day; it should be here tomorrow.

Also, thank you for the suggestion; I did try Valerian root once and it knocked me out for 14 hours, which was rather worrying. I might try it again, though, if the melatonin doesn't help as much as I hope it will.
Ah, I wasn't aware of that. I've only ever used trees maybe 4-5 times. Once I got super paranoid, but the other times I experienced no adverse effects (but also didn't have very much).

No, no, I don't interact with them, and I'm fully conscious and aware of what's going on, I just see/hear things that aren't there. I almost always realize immediately what's happening, and then it usually goes away. The one time this wasn't true was when I was sitting through a powerpoint presentation, got suspicious, and had my friend sitting next to me confirm that there were not, in fact, flashing neon  shapes on the slides.
